title: Reject Self Help Slop. Embrace the Great Man Biography.
author: Thinking West
summary: Thinking West argues that modern self-help fails because it traps readers inside their own heads, analyzing flaws and optimizing routines until they overthink every step. The proposed remedy is to read about others, specifically the biographies of great men of history, which show what a person is capable of rather than offering contrived life hacks. Three reasons are given: biographies pull you out of your head into an adventurous life, using Marcus Aurelius as the example of a thinker who chose action; they give a long perspective, as with Julius Caesar, who felt himself a failure at thirty; and they are grounded in reality, showing the faults of figures such as Churchill and Alexander alongside their triumphs. The piece closes with recommended titles, including works by Philip Freeman, Andrew Roberts, Plutarch and the Gospels.
points: Self-help can become a form of procrastination because it invites endless self-analysis, whereas a biography redirects attention to action and achievement.
Marcus Aurelius wrote the Meditations on campaign and scolded himself for lingering in philosophy, which the author offers as proof that contemplation must end in action.
Biographies provide a long perspective on cause and effect across a lifetime, showing decades of failure preceding breakthroughs, as with Caesar, who wept at Alexander's tomb at about thirty.
Because biographies record faults along with triumphs, they make greatness look more accessible and remove the excuse of waiting for perfect timing.
The reading list pairs concise modern biographies with Plutarch's Lives as a way to sample many characters quickly.
quotes: Modern self help books fail for a single reason: they trap you inside your own head.
The single greatest self-improvement tool you can own, then, is a biography. It shows you a real life example of what a person is capable of rather than a list of contrived “life hacks.
Overthinking is one of the most detrimental habits that can stifle a person’s personal development. It makes you constantly question every decision, paralyzing you until you just feel stuck.
Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
There’s nothing wrong with deep contemplation, of course, but when it becomes a means of procrastination, it starts looking a little more like cowardice than prudence.

Rather than a list of neatly packaged life hacks, biographies offer a holistic representation of a great person: how decades of failure laid the groundwork for a sudden breakthrough; how early arrogance caused ruin and a recalibration; or how effort and patience paid off in the long run.
By the age of 30, he hadn’t accomplished anything notable, and believed himself to be a failure. When he visited Alexander the Great’s tomb, he wept.
Biographies are narratives of what actually happened rather than advertisements getting you to buy into a certain way of doing things.
